cards.text: Jesus just told His disciples that some of them would see the kingdom of God arrive with power. Six days later, He takes three of them up a high mountain. Just them. Nobody else.

cards.question: Jesus leads three of His disciples up a high mountain by themselves. Which three?

cards.text: Up on that mountain, right in front of them, Jesus is transfigured. I bet they did NOT see that coming when they started the hike.

cards.question: On the mountain, Jesus' clothes become radiantly ___, brighter than any launderer on earth could bleach them.

cards.text: Friend, I've worn a white apron my whole baking life, and I have NEVER gotten it that white. Then two more people appear on that mountain, talking with Jesus.

cards.question: Two men appear on the high mountain and talk with Jesus. Who are they?

cards.text: Elijah the prophet and Moses, Israel's leader, right there with Jesus. And Peter opens his mouth: "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here."

cards.question: Peter tells Jesus it is good for them to be on the mountain. What does Peter offer to put up?
Peter offers to put up a shelter for Jesus, one for Moses and one for Elijah. Why does Peter say this?

answers.text: They were so terrified he didn't know what else to say
He hoped Moses and Elijah would stay on the mountain for good
He wanted all Israel to remember the place where it happened

cards.text: Friend, I get it: when I'm scared, my mouth starts meetings my brain NEVER approved. Then a cloud appears and wraps around them, and a voice comes from the cloud.

cards.question: The voice from the cloud says, "This is My beloved ___. Listen to Him!"
After the voice speaks, the disciples suddenly look around. Moses and Elijah are still standing there with Jesus.

cards.text: Now it's just Jesus with Peter, James and John, heading back down the mountain. On the way, Jesus gives them firm instructions about what they've seen.

cards.question: Coming down the mountain, what does Jesus tell the three disciples to do about what they saw?

answers.text: Tell no one until the Son of Man has risen from the dead
Tell the other disciples as soon as they get back down
Tell the crowds in every village they pass through

cards.question: The three disciples keep the matter to themselves. What do they discuss among themselves?

answers.text: What it meant to rise from the dead
Which one of them was the greatest
Where Moses and Elijah had gone

cards.text: Imagine seeing THAT and keeping it out of every group chat you're in. Then they bring Jesus a question about something the scribes, Israel's teachers of the law, say about Elijah.

cards.question: The disciples ask Jesus about the scribes' teaching. What do the scribes say about Elijah?

cards.text: Jesus says Elijah does indeed come first, and he restores all things. Then Jesus asks a question right back, about what is written of the Son of Man.

cards.question: Jesus asks His disciples a question about the Son of Man. What does Jesus say is written about Him?

answers.text: He must suffer many things and be rejected
He must rule over all the nations at once
He must stay hidden from every crowd

cards.question: Jesus tells Peter, James and John that Elijah has already come, and people did to him whatever they wished.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 11 quotes "This is My beloved ___. Listen to Him!", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: "Jesus just told...", "Six days later...", "Just them." and "Nobody else." The limit is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus "told His disciples" that "some of them" would see the kingdom come with power. Mark 9:1 says "some of those standing here," and the audience in Mark 8:34 is the crowd along with His disciples. The card narrows who was spoken to beyond what the text says.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke ("I bet they did NOT see that coming when they started the hike") is a mild, pleasant line rather than a real laugh, and this is a moment that could hold one.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The question says the clothes are "brighter than any launderer on earth could bleach them." Bleaching only makes things white, so this wording rules out "golden" and "crimson" and gives the answer away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "He hoped Moses and Elijah would stay on the mountain for good" is arguable. Offering to put up shelters for Moses and Elijah can reasonably be read as wanting them to stay, so a baker could argue it is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to supply the exact word in the voice's line ("My beloved ___"). Nothing earlier sets up a way to reason to "Son" over "Prophet" or "Servant", so the card tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "He must rule over all the nations at once" is arguably written about the Son of Man elsewhere in Scripture (Daniel 7:13-14 gives Him dominion over all peoples and nations). A baker could argue it is right. The phrase "at once" also makes it sound off next to the other answers.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
